328	def profile(crossings, tolerances):
329	    """Build a tolerance profile from :func:`audit` results.
330	
331	    Calls :func:`audit` exactly once with ``crossings`` and
332	    ``tolerances``, so its validation, first-error order, exceptions
333	    (propagated unchanged) and index prefixes all apply here as well.
334	    Inputs are not modified.
335	
336	    With ``R`` the tuple returned by :func:`audit`, one item per input
337	    tolerance, items are ordered ascending by
338	    ``(tolerances[i], i)``; equal tolerances therefore keep their input
339	    order. ``curve`` is a tuple of dicts, one per ordered item, each
340	    with keys in the order
341	    ``tolerance, within_tolerance, within_ratio, bias, rmse,
342	    quality``; ``tolerance`` is ``round(float(tolerances[i]), 6)``
343	    (negative zero normalized to ``0.0``) and the remaining fields are
344	    copied unchanged from the corresponding ``R`` item.
345	
346	    ``monotonic`` is whether the ``within_tolerance`` counts are
347	    non-decreasing along the curve (``True`` for a single item).
348	    ``first_pass_tolerance`` is the rounded threshold of the first
349	    curve item whose ``quality`` is ``"pass"``, or ``None`` when no
350	    item passes.
351	
352	    With ``t_i`` the *unrounded* tolerance and ``q_i`` the
353	    ``within_ratio`` of the item at ordered position ``i`` and
354	    ``m = len(R)``, ``area`` is ``0.0`` for ``m < 2`` and otherwise the
355	    trapezoidal integral
356	    ``round(float(fsum((t_i - t_{i-1}) * (q_i + q_{i-1}) / 2
357	    for i in range(1, m))), 6)`` with negative zero normalized to
358	    ``0.0``.
359	
360	    Returns a dict with keys in the order
361	    ``curve, monotonic, first_pass_tolerance, area``; their types are
362	    tuple, bool, float or ``None`` and float.
363	    """
364	    reports = audit(crossings, tolerances)
365	    return _profile_from_reports(reports, tolerances)

368	def _aggregate_from_reports(reports, tolerances):
369	    """Compute the :func:`aggregate` result from an :func:`audit` tuple."""
370	    m = len(reports)
371	
372	    count = sum(x["count"] for x in reports)
373	    pass_count = sum(x["quality"] == "pass" for x in reports)
374	    fail_count = m - pass_count
375	    mean_bias = math.fsum(x["bias"] for x in reports) / m
376	    max_rmse = max(x["rmse"] for x in reports)
377	    mean_ratio = math.fsum(x["within_ratio"] for x in reports) / m
378	
379	    passed = [t for t, x in zip(tolerances, reports) if x["quality"] == "pass"]
380	    best_tolerance = min(passed) if passed else None
381	
382	    result = {
383	        "count": int(count),
384	        "pass_count": int(pass_count),
385	        "fail_count": int(fail_count),
386	    }
387	    for name, value in (
388	        ("mean_bias", mean_bias),
389	        ("max_rmse", max_rmse),
390	        ("mean_ratio", mean_ratio),
391	    ):
392	        value = round(float(value), 6)
393	        result[name] = 0.0 if value == 0 else value
394	    if best_tolerance is None:
395	        result["best_tolerance"] = None
396	    else:
397	        best_tolerance = round(float(best_tolerance), 6)
398	        result["best_tolerance"] = 0.0 if best_tolerance == 0 else best_tolerance
399	    result["quality"] = "pass" if pass_count == m else "fail"
400	    return result

408	    unchanged) and per-tolerance reports all apply here as well.

426	    decimals (negative zero normalized to ``0.0``).

432	def dashboard(crossings, tolerances):
433	    """Bundle :func:`audit`, :func:`profile` and :func:`aggregate` results.
434	
435	    Calls :func:`audit` exactly once with ``crossings`` and
436	    ``tolerances``, so its validation, first-error order, exceptions
437	    (propagated unchanged) and index prefixes all apply here as well.
438	    Inputs are not modified; :func:`profile` and :func:`aggregate` are
439	    not called (their values are derived directly from the single
440	    :func:`audit` result).
441	
442	    Returns a tuple ``(reports, profile, aggregate, quality)`` where
443	    ``reports`` is the tuple returned by :func:`audit`; ``profile`` and
444	    ``aggregate`` are dicts with the keys, values, types and rounding
445	    rules of :func:`profile` and :func:`aggregate` respectively; and
446	    ``quality`` is ``"pass"`` only when the aggregate ``quality`` is
447	    ``"pass"``, the profile ``monotonic`` flag is true and
448	    ``first_pass_tolerance`` is not ``None``, and ``"fail"`` otherwise.
449	    """
450	    reports = audit(crossings, tolerances)
451	    profiled = _profile_from_reports(reports, tolerances)
452	    aggregated = _aggregate_from_reports(reports, tolerances)
453	    quality = (
454	        "pass"
455	        if aggregated["quality"] == "pass"
456	        and profiled["monotonic"] is True
457	        and profiled["first_pass_tolerance"] is not None
458	        else "fail"
459	    )
460	    return reports, profiled, aggregated, quality

463	def dashboard_summary(crossings, tolerances):
464	    """Summarize crosspoint depth differences across tolerances.
465	
466	    ``crossings`` is a non-empty list/tuple; each item is a
467	    four-element list/tuple ``(x, y, d1, d2)`` whose fields are finite
468	    non-bool int/float values, with ``d1, d2 >= 0``. ``tolerances``
469	    must then be a non-empty list/tuple whose items, checked in input
470	    order, are finite non-bool int/float values ``> 0``.
471	
472	    Validation order (first error wins): the ``crossings`` container,
473	    its non-emptiness, each crossing in index order (item container,
474	    length, fields), then the ``tolerances`` container, its
475	    non-emptiness, then each tolerance in index order (type,
476	    finiteness, positivity). Type mismatches raise ``TypeError``; every
477	    other violation raises ``ValueError``. Item errors are prefixed
478	    with ``"crossings[i]: "`` or ``"tolerances[i]: "``.
479	
480	    With ``r = d1 - d2``, ``n`` the number of crosspoints and each
481	    tolerance ``t``, the per-tolerance statistics are
482	    ``b = fsum(r) / n`` (mean bias), ``e = sqrt(fsum(r**2) / n)``
483	    (RMSE), ``w`` the number of crosspoints with ``abs(r) <= t`` and
484	    ``q = w / n``; the tolerance passes (``p``) when ``w == n``.
485	
486	    Returns a dict with keys in the order
487	    ``count, pass_count, fail_count, total_count, mean_bias, max_rmse,
488	    mean_ratio, quality``; ``count`` is the number of tolerances;
489	    ``pass_count``/``fail_count`` are the numbers of tolerances for
490	    which ``p`` is true/false; ``total_count`` is the sum of ``n`` over
491	    the tolerances; ``mean_bias`` is the mean of the ``b`` values,
492	    ``max_rmse`` the maximum of the ``e`` values and ``mean_ratio`` the
493	    mean of the ``q`` values; ``quality`` is ``"pass"`` only when every
494	    tolerance passes and ``"fail"`` otherwise. Counts are ints and the
495	    statistics are floats rounded to 6 decimals (negative zero
496	    normalized to ``0.0``). Inputs are not modified.
497	    """
498	    _validate_crossings(crossings)
499	    _validate_tolerances(tolerances)
500	
501	    differences = [d1 - d2 for x, y, d1, d2 in crossings]
502	    n = len(differences)
503	    m = len(tolerances)
504	
505	    biases = []
506	    rmses = []
507	    ratios = []
508	    pass_count = 0
509	    for tolerance in tolerances:
510	        bias = math.fsum(differences) / n
511	        rmse = math.sqrt(math.fsum(r * r for r in differences) / n)
512	        within = sum(1 for r in differences if abs(r) <= tolerance)
513	        biases.append(bias)
514	        rmses.append(rmse)
515	        ratios.append(within / n)
516	        if within == n:
517	            pass_count += 1
518	
519	    fail_count = m - pass_count
520	    mean_bias = math.fsum(biases) / m
521	    max_rmse = max(rmses)
522	    mean_ratio = math.fsum(ratios) / m
523	
524	    result = {
525	        "count": int(m),
526	        "pass_count": int(pass_count),
527	        "fail_count": int(fail_count),
528	        "total_count": int(n * m),
529	    }
530	    for name, value in (
531	        ("mean_bias", mean_bias),
532	        ("max_rmse", max_rmse),
533	        ("mean_ratio", mean_ratio),
534	    ):
535	        value = round(float(value), 6)
536	        result[name] = 0.0 if value == 0 else value
537	    result["quality"] = "pass" if pass_count == m else "fail"
538	    return result

541	def dashboard_report(crossings, tolerances):
542	    """Bundle :func:`dashboard` with a cross-tolerance summary.
543	
544	    Calls :func:`dashboard` exactly once with ``crossings`` and
545	    ``tolerances``, so its validation, first-error order, exceptions
546	    (propagated unchanged) and index prefixes all apply here as well.
547	    Inputs and the :func:`dashboard` result are not modified.
548	
549	    With ``D`` the four-tuple returned by :func:`dashboard`, ``R`` its
550	    first item (the per-tolerance reports) and ``m = len(R)``, the
551	    summary is ``count = m``, ``pass_count`` the number of reports with
552	    ``quality == "pass"``, ``fail_count = m - pass_count``,
553	    ``total_count = sum(x["count"])``,
554	    ``mean_bias = fsum(x["bias"]) / m``,
555	    ``max_rmse = max(x["rmse"])`` and
556	    ``mean_ratio = fsum(x["within_ratio"]) / m``.
557	    ``best_tolerance`` is the smallest tolerance whose report passed,
558	    or ``None`` when no report passed, and ``quality_score`` is
559	    ``100 * (pass_count / m) * mean_ratio``.
560	
561	    Returns a dict with keys in the order ``dashboard, summary,
562	    quality``; ``dashboard`` is ``D`` itself and ``quality`` is
563	    ``D[3]``. ``summary`` is a dict with keys in the order ``count,
564	    pass_count, fail_count, total_count, mean_bias, max_rmse,
565	    mean_ratio, best_tolerance, quality_score``; the counts are ints,
566	    ``best_tolerance`` is a float or ``None`` and the remaining
567	    statistics are floats rounded to 6 decimals (negative zero
568	    normalized to ``0.0``).
569	    """
570	    result = dashboard(crossings, tolerances)
571	    reports = result[0]
572	    m = len(reports)
573

718	def pair(first, second, tolerance=1.0):
719	    """Pair points from two surveys at coincident locations.

722	    point is a three-element list/tuple ``(x, y, d)`` whose fields are
723	    finite non-bool int/float values, with ``d >= 0``. ``tolerance``
724	    must be a finite non-bool int/float ``> 0``.
725	
726	    Each ``first`` point is processed in input order and matched to the
727	    still-unused ``second`` point minimizing the unrounded 2-D distance
728	    ``sqrt((x1 - x2)**2 + (y1 - y2)**2)``, provided it does not exceed
729	    ``tolerance``; equal distances resolve to the earliest ``second``
730	    point in input order. A ``first`` point with no admissible match is
731	    skipped, and a ``second`` point can be used at most once. If fewer
732	    than one pair is formed, a ``ValueError`` is raised.
733	
734	    Validation order (first error wins): the ``first`` container, its
735	    non-emptiness, the ``second`` container, its non-emptiness, each
736	    point in index order (first ``first`` points then ``second`` points:
737	    point container, length, fields), then ``tolerance`` (type,
738	    finiteness, positivity). Point errors are prefixed with
739	    ``"first[i]: "`` or ``"second[j]: "``.
740

742	    ``(x, y, d1, d2)`` whose items are all floats; ``x``/``y`` and
743	    ``d1`` come from the ``first`` point and ``d2`` from the matched
744	    ``second`` point. Values are rounded to 6 decimals (negative zero
745	    normalized to ``0.0``). Inputs are not modified.
746	    """
747	    if not isinstance(first, (list, tuple)):
748	        raise TypeError("first must be a list or tuple")
749	    if len(first) == 0:
750	        raise ValueError("first must be non-empty")
751	    if not isinstance(second, (list, tuple)):
752	        raise TypeError("second must be a list or tuple")
753	    if len(second) == 0:
754	        raise ValueError("second must be non-empty")
755	
756	    for label, points in (("first", first), ("second", second)):
757	        for i in range(len(points)):
758	            point = points[i]
759	            prefix = f"{label}[{i}]: "
760	            if not isinstance(point, (list, tuple)):
761	                raise TypeError(prefix + "must be a list or tuple")
762	            if len(point) != 3:
763	                raise ValueError(prefix + "must have 3 elements")
764	            for name, value in zip(_POINT_FIELDS, point):
765	                if not _is_real_number(value):
766	                    raise TypeError(prefix + f"{name} must be a non-bool int or float")
767	            for name, value in zip(_POINT_FIELDS, point):
768	                if not math.isfinite(value):
769	                    raise ValueError(prefix + f"{name} must be finite")
770	            if not point[2] >= 0:
771	                raise ValueError(prefix + "d must be >= 0")
772	
773	    if not _is_real_number(tolerance):
774	        raise TypeError("tolerance must be a non-bool int or float")
775	    if not math.isfinite(tolerance):
776	        raise ValueError("tolerance must be finite")
777	    if not tolerance > 0:
778	        raise ValueError("tolerance must be > 0")
779	
780	    used = [False] * len(second)
781	    pairs = []
782	    for x1, y1, d1 in first:
783	        best_index = None
784	        best_distance = None
785	        for j in range(len(second)):
786	            if used[j]:
787	                continue
788	            x2, y2, d2 = second[j]
789	            distance = math.sqrt((x1 - x2) ** 2 + (y1 - y2) ** 2)
790	            if distance <= tolerance and (
791	                best_distance is None or distance < best_distance
792	            ):
793	                best_index = j
794	                best_distance = distance
795	        if best_index is None:
796	            continue
797	        used[best_index] = True
798	        x2, y2, d2 = second[best_index]

800	
801	    if len(pairs) == 0:
802	        raise ValueError("no points matched within tolerance")
803	
804	    result = []
805	    for x, y, d1, d2 in pairs:
806	        item = []
807	        for value in (x, y, d1, d2):
808	            rounded = round(float(value), 6)
809	            item.append(0.0 if rounded == 0 else rounded)
810	        result.append(tuple(item))
811	    return tuple(result)

1234	) -> str:

1248	    is propagated unchanged. Inputs are not modified.

1254	    ``w`` the smallest index minimizing ``(S_i, C_i, i)`` lexicographically,
1255	    returns one line with no trailing newline::
1256	
1257	        count=n;mean_score=s;worst_index=w;quality=q
1258

1260	    negative zero normalized to ``0.0``, ``n`` and ``w`` are rendered in

1262	    otherwise.

1267	        raise ValueError("records must be non-empty")
1268	    for i in range(len(records)):
1269	        record = records[i]
1270	        prefix = f"records[{i}]: "
1271	        if not isinstance(record, (list, tuple)):
1272	            raise TypeError(prefix + "must be a list or tuple")
1273	        if len(record) != 2:
1274	            raise ValueError(prefix + "must have 2 elements")

1277	    coverages = []

1281	            first, second, tolerances, 1.0, min_coverage, min_score
1282	        )

1284	        coverages.append(inner["summary"]["coverage_product"])
1285	        scores.append(inner["score_report"]["score_report"]["score"])

1299	        f"count={n};"

1316	    two-element lists/tuples. A non-list/tuple container raises

1318	    Item errors are prefixed with ``"records[i]: "``.

1322	    ``1.0``, ``min_coverage`` and ``min_score``; any exception it raises
1323	    is propagated unchanged. Inputs are not modified.

1326	    ``P = R["report"]["report"]``,
1327	    ``C = P["summary"]["coverage_product"]``,
1328	    ``S = P["score_report"]["score_report"]["score"]`` and
1329	    ``Q = R["quality"]``, the worst index ``w`` minimizes the
1330	    *unrounded* tuple ``(S, C, i)`` lexicographically, the mean score is

1339	    order ``records, summary``. ``records`` is an array whose items have
1340	    keys in the order ``index, coverage, score, quality`` with values

1342	    has keys in the order ``count, mean_score, worst_index, quality``
1343	    with values ``n``, the mean score, ``w`` and the batch quality.

1345	    ``separators=(",", ":")``, ``allow_nan=False``), six-decimal float
1346	    rounding with negative zero normalized to ``0.0``, the absence of a
1347	    trailing newline and the ``ValueError`` raised on any JSON or UTF-8

1349	    :func:`serialize_pair_gate_score_summary`.

1353	    if not isinstance(records, (list, tuple)):

1358	        record = records[i]
1359	        prefix = f"records[{i}]: "
1360	        if not isinstance(record, (list, tuple)):

1363	            raise ValueError(prefix + "must have 2 elements")
1364

1366	    raw_scores = []
1367	    qualities = []
1368	    for first, second in records:
1369	        result = pair_gate_quality_report(
1370	            first, second, tolerances, 1.0, min_coverage, min_score
1371	        )
1372	        inner = result["report"]["report"]
1373	        raw_coverages.append(inner["summary"]["coverage_product"])
1374	        raw_scores.append(inner["score_report"]["score_report"]["score"])

1382	        range(n), key=lambda i: (raw_scores[i], raw_coverages[i], i)
1383	    )

1392	            score = 0.0
